Draw the Panel Matrix of a Multivariate Density

Source: R/mv_plot.R
mv_pairs_panels.Rd

This function is the shared engine of plot.multivariate_distrib() and the multivariate branch of plot.distrib_fit(). It lays out one panel per ordered pair of the chosen coordinates: the marginal density on the diagonal, contours of the bivariate marginal below it, and the implied correlation printed above it. The density panels come from mv_marginal(), so the function does not integrate anything; the printed correlation comes from mv_sigma().

Usage

mv_pairs_panels(
  d,
  theta,
  which,
  n_grid,
  col_fit,
  data,
  col_data = "#4682B4",
  which_arg = "which",
  ...
)

Arguments

d

A multivariate_distrib() object.

theta

A named list of parameters, already aligned by the caller.

which

An integer vector of distinct coordinates, or NULL for all of them. An empty, non-integer, out-of-range or duplicated which, or more than three coordinates, is an error.

n_grid

Points per axis, a single positive whole number.

col_fit

Color of the fitted density, the contours and the printed correlations.

data

An \(n \times p\) matrix of observations with one column per coordinate of the distribution, whichever coordinates which selects, or NULL for a distribution with no data behind it.

col_data

Color of the observed summary, used only when data is given. Defaults to "#4682B4".

which_arg

The name of the caller's argument that carries which, used in the error message for more than three coordinates. Defaults to "which"; plot.distrib_fit() passes "mv_which".

...

Unused.

Value

NULL, invisibly. The function is called for the plot that it draws. The function sets mfrow, mar and mgp for the panel matrix and restores the previous values on exit.

Details

When data is supplied the diagonal also carries a kernel density estimate of the observed coordinate and the panels below the diagonal carry the observations, so the fitted shape and the sample are read against each other in one frame. The panels above the diagonal show only the correlation. The kernel estimate (stats::density()) does not depend on the fitted family and serves as a model-free comparison.

Each coordinate is drawn over three standard deviations either side of the location, widened when data is supplied to include the observations. The spread is taken from mv_sigma(), so a Student \(t\) with \(\nu \le 2\) still has a finite range, where variance() returns an infinite matrix.

See also

plot.multivariate_distrib() and plot.distrib_fit(), its two callers, and mv_marginal() for the panels.

Examples

d <- mvgaussian1_distrib(2)
theta <- list(mu1 = 0, mu2 = 0, sigma_log_L1 = 0,
              sigma_log_L2 = 0, sigma_L2.1 = 0.6)

# Without data, the plot shows the density alone.
op <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
distributions7:::mv_pairs_panels(d, theta, NULL, 40, "#B22222", data = NULL)

graphics::par(op)

# With data: the same frame carries a kernel estimate and the observations.
set.seed(1)
op <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
distributions7:::mv_pairs_panels(d, theta, NULL, 40, "#B22222",
                                 data = distrib_rng(d, 200, theta))

graphics::par(op)
